summary:
NusaShift is an interactive Earth-system trend detective web application built on 40 years (1985-2025) of NASA POWER v2 satellite telemetry (MERRA-2, CERES, GPM IMERG) and cross-validated against NASA GISTEMP v4. Through a click-anywhere 3D globe and 2D analytical map, users can compare any two regions on Earth to investigate long-term climate regime shifts.

To address the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge, NusaShift removes seasonal monsoon noise using monthly Z-score deseasonalization and applies non-parametric Mann-Kendall significance tests, Sen's Slope trends, Pettitt change-point detection, and 0-6 month water-energy lag-cascade analysis. It translates complex satellite telemetry into both a symptom-first Citizen View and a transparent Scientific Proof matrix, paired with an evidence-bound AI causal brief.

This matters because single-region rainfall charts often overlook cross-oceanic teleconnections and "Silent Ecological Stress", where root-zone soil moisture declines months before precipitation drops. NusaShift empowers researchers, educators, and communities to detect climate shifts earlier.
details:
What NusaShift Does & How It Works

NusaShift is a web-based Earth-system trend detective designed for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Users explore a click-anywhere 3D interactive globe (with a 2D analytical map fallback) featuring country boundaries and reverse-geocoded place names to select any two regions on Earth, or load three curated teleconnection cases across 40 years (1985-2025) of monthly satellite data.

Once two regions are selected, the backend fetches 5 coupled variables from NASA POWER v2 (Solar Surface Irradiance, Root-Zone Soil Wetness, Earth Skin Temperature, Bias-Corrected Precipitation, and 2m Air Temperature) and runs a deterministic statistical pipeline:

1. Monthly Z-score deseasonalization to remove recurring monsoon cycles.

2. Non-parametric Mann-Kendall trend testing (tau, Z-score, p-value) and Sen's Slope with 95% confidence intervals.

3. Pettitt change-point detection to pinpoint the exact year and month a climate regime shift began.

4. Water-energy lag-cascade cross-correlation (0-6 months) to detect "Silent Ecological Stress", where root-zone soil wetness declines significantly before rainfall totals show a statistically significant drop.

5. Cross-validation against NASA GISTEMP v4 global land-ocean temperature records (1985-2025).

Benefits & Intended Impact

NusaShift bridges the gap between raw satellite telemetry and real-world decision making. Citizens, students, and local planners can start from observable symptoms (Coastal Drought, Peatland Drying, Flood Dipole) in the Citizen View, while climate researchers can inspect the full statistical audit table, GISTEMP v4 benchmark alignment, and KaTeX-typeset formulas in the Scientific Proof drawer. Early detection of root-zone drying and cross-oceanic teleconnections helps agricultural, peatland, and disaster-mitigation teams respond months earlier.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered

- Dual-Layer Accessibility: Combines plain-language symptom triage with formal non-parametric statistics and shareable/exportable briefs.

- Zero-Hallucination Bounded AI: Uses Google Gemini only to synthesize explanations strictly locked to computed statistics, with an automatic deterministic physics-based fallback if offline or unconfigured.

- Graceful Offline & Ocean Handling: Filters NASA POWER -999 ocean/missing values, uses real reverse-geocoding for coordinate context, and provides precomputed real-data fallback for instant demos.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

- Frontend & Framework: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4

- 3D Globe & Data Visualization: Three.js, react-globe.gl, TopoJSON (Natural Earth 110m), Recharts, KaTeX, Lucide Icons

- Data & AI Services: NASA POWER API v2 (MERRA-2, CERES, GPM IMERG), NASA GISTEMP v4, BigDataCloud reverse geocoding, Google GenAI SDK (Gemini)
